points.ref: Evely, D. 2012. RODA-ACHARAVIS - 2002. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 3294; after Zernioti (Η' ΕΠΚΑ).
points.note: R188 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and KML coordinates; source says 'Hellenistic probable olive oil workshop', so confidence is medium and wording remains probable. | R188B period vocabulary repair: Hellenistic source label mapped to canonical period=classical.

points.dm: Chronique/EFA reports an antique olive m
points.ref: Decavallas, O. 2021. DOKOS. Gyrismata - 1983. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 16892; excerpt from BCH 114.2 (1990), p. 733.
points.note: R188 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and KML coordinates; date is cautious because source says antique olive millstone plus Late Empire pottery and older stray finds.

points.s: Vassiliki (Ierapetra), Room 30 olive kernel under paving
points.ref: Decavallas, O. 2021. VASSILIKI (HIERAPETRA) - 1991. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 14932; after Ergon (1991) [1992], pp. 109-110 and BCH 116.2 (1992), pp. 935-937.
points.note: R188 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and KML coordinates; row records the olive kernel itself, not the broader source claim about 5,500 years of local cultivation continuity.

points.s: Papadiokambos house A.1/B.1 carbonized olive plant remains
points.ref: Morgan, C. 2010. PAPADIOKAMBOS - 2008. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 761; unpublished field report C. Sophianou.
points.note: R189 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and public KML coordinates. Source also suggests small-scale olive oil and wine production in houses, but row records only direct carbonized Olea plant remains.

points.s: Karthaia Koulas room A late Hellenistic olive pits
points.ref: Bouras, C. 2011. KEA - Karthaia - 2010. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 2071; after E. Simantoni-Bournia, University of Athens archaeology department activity report.
points.note: R189 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and public KML coordinates; row records direct olive pits only, not oil production.

points.s: Kydonia / Chania chamber tomb calcined olive kernel
points.ref: Samara, S. 2021. LA CANEE - 1991. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 14487; extract from Pariente, BCH 118.2 (1994), pp. 836-837.
points.note: R189 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and public KML coordinates. Source also reports poros oil-press elements in the same fourth-century BCE reused chamber, but row records only the direct olive kernel to avoid over-counting press installations in a dense Chania coordinate cluster.

points.s: Archanes Building 4 vessel with olive stones
points.ref: Dewulf, E. 2026. ARCHANES - 1977. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 21662; extract from Touchais, BCH 102.2 (1978), pp. 758-760.
points.note: R189 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and public KML coordinates. The adjacent installation is described as a wine press, so row records only the vessel with olive stones.

points.s: Delos Agora des Competaliastes olive pit assemblage
points.ref: Bouras, C. 2022. DELOS - Agora des Competaliastes - 2020. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 17399; after Cl. Pagnoux mission report to Delos in 2020.
points.note: R189 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and public KML coordinates. Distinct from broad Delos trade/storage row exp_068 and OXREP/iDAI press rows; use as direct macroremain assemblage only.

points.s: Diros Alepotrypa cave Late Neolithic olive leaves
points.dm: Chronique/EFA reports the three olive le
points.ref: Decavallas, O. 2021. DIROS. - Alepotrypa et Katafyghi - 1988. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 16941; extract from BCH 113.2 (1989), p. 610.
points.note: R190 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and map point coordinates. This is direct Olea leaf presence in a Neolithic archaeological level, not evidence for oil production or cultivation intensity.

points.s: Thera Fira caldera fossil Olea europaea leaves
points.ref: Samara, S. 2021. THERA - Fyra - 2000. Chronique des fouilles en ligne / Archaeology in Greece Online, record 11501; extract from Touchais, Huber, Philippa-Touchais, BCH 125.2 (2001), p. 997.
points.note: R190 strict append from official Chronique/EFA page and map point coordinates. Use as palaeoenvironmental Olea presence only; not archaeological cultivation, domestication, production, or oil evidence. | R190B period vocabulary repair: ca. 50,000 BC fossil Olea presence mapped to canonical period=prehistoric.

points.st: charred olive stones in ritual hearths
points.rg: Sozopol / Apollonia Pontica / western Black Sea coast
points.ref: Popova, Tz. 2022. New archaeobotanical evidence about Olea europaea subsp. europaea from the territory of Bulgaria. Interdisciplinary Studies XXVII:43-58, Table 1.
points.note: R192 granular split from Popova 2022 Table 1: Kalfata UPI 5258 hearth 4 has 1 whole Olea europaea subsp. europaea stone; UPI 5098 hearth 2 has 2 fragments/halves. Coordinates are inherited as the existing Sozopol regional centroid, not a feature GPS point.

points.s: Sikyon plain, Classical to early Hellenistic olive stones
points.ref: Tsirtsi, K. et al. 2023. Development of olive cultivation at the site of Sikyon, Greece: evidence from the charred olive remains from the late Classical/early Hellenistic to the Roman period. Vegetation History and Archaeobotany 32.
points.note: R192 replaces broad h1750_0056 with phase-level quantified rows. Source text: plain contexts in five trenches provided 65 olive stones, mostly Classical, with one Hellenistic burial context and some Roman contexts in Field 8.

points.s: Sikyon plateau agora Roman olive stones
points.rg: Corinthia / northeastern Peloponnese / Sikyon plateau agora
points.ref: Tsirtsi, K. et al. 2023. Development of olive cultivation at the site of Sikyon, Greece: evidence from the charred olive remains from the late Classical/early Hellenistic to the Roman period. Vegetation History and Archaeobotany 32.
points.note: R192 replaces broad h1750_0056 with phase-level quantified rows. Source text: plateau contexts produced 104 olive stones, with kiln/workshop contexts around late 1st-early 2nd c. CE and 5th/6th c. CE deposits.
